newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK SLOVAKOFARMA SAYS PREPARING GDR ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK SLOVAKOFARMA SAYS PREPARING GDR ISSUE.

text.p: Slovakia's largest drug maker Slovakofarma a.s. said on Monday it was preparing to launch an unspecified tranche of global depositary receipts (GDR) later this year.
"We expect the details of the issue will be completed by the annual shareholders' meeting in May," Tibor Velky of Slovakofarma's capital investment department told Reuters.
According to the proposal, the company will issue 230,765 bearer shares at a nominal value of 1,000 crowns which would be convertible into GDRs.
Slovakofarma's AGM has been scheduled for May 15.
"However, the preparatory work (on the issue) will take at least several months," Velky said.
Capital market players said the issue was expected to help revive the currently lean Slovak market as well as to improve the performance of Slovakofarma itself.
"The issue should increase the liquidity of Slovakofarma and perhaps help re-attract overall investor interest," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.
"I think foreign players will mostly respond positively to the possibility of converting these shares into GDRs," he added.
But it was still undecided which part of the entire issue will be allowed to be converted, he said.
"It would be too early to talk about such details at the moment," Velky said.
Slovakofarma, currently the most expensive Slovak share, has been suffering from low liquidity on the bourse over the last few months.
It traded 1,000 shares on the Bratislava Stock Exchange's unlisted market on Friday, and closed down 210 crowns, at 4,000.
The share price has been gradually but consistently falling from February's 5,200 crown high, after it had jumped from last year's level of around 2,800 crowns at the beginning of the year.
Slovakofarma said in February that it expected an after-tax profit of around 500 million crowns for 1996, compared with a 481.2 million crown net profit in 1995.
Slovakofarma officials said the company planned to pay a dividend of "around" 200 crowns per share compared with 250 crowns on 1995 profits.
